segments.text: OK, I think we have everyone except Arjun, he said he'll join around half past. Can everyone hear me?
Yes, loud and clear.
Yes.

Great. So as I mentioned in the invite, this is the first discovery call for the AP invoice processing assessment. The CoE wants to understand how invoices flow today for the India entity, where the pain is, and whether automation makes sense at all, and where. Nothing is decided yet. Meera, maybe you can start with the big picture?

Sure. So I manage accounts payable for Kaveri Industrial Components, the India entity, company code 1000 in SAP. We are a shared services team here in Pune. Six AP clerks, one team lead, that's Karthik, he couldn't make it today, and me. We process all vendor invoices for the India business, both PO and non-PO.
And roughly what volumes are we talking about?

Last few months it has been around nine to ten thousand invoices a month. It goes up at quarter end. Around eighty percent are against purchase orders, the remaining twenty percent are non-PO, things like utilities, rent, professional fees, some services.
OK. And how do invoices come in to you?

Most vendors email the PDF to the shared mailbox, ap.invoices at kaveri-ic dot example. Some smaller vendors still send paper by courier to the Pune office. I would say ten to fifteen percent is paper, honestly nobody has counted it properly. When paper comes, one of us scans it on the office scanner and it lands back in the same mailbox as a PDF.
So everything ends up in the mailbox.
Yes, everything.
Sunita, could you walk me through what you do with one invoice, say a normal PO invoice with no problem?

OK. First I open the email, I save the PDF into the SharePoint library, we have a folder per vendor in the AP Invoices library. Then I make an entry in the tracker, it's an Excel file on SharePoint, AP tracker FY27. Vendor name, invoice number, invoice date, amount, PO number if there is one, date received, and status. Then I check the invoice itself, whether it has everything. Our legal name and GSTIN, the vendor GSTIN, invoice number and date, PO number, HSN or SAC codes, the tax breakup. If something is missing we send it back to the vendor with a standard email.
Is that check written down somewhere, the list of mandatory fields?
Yes, it's in the SOP, section six point three I think. I'll share the SOP after the call.

Then I go to SAP and check the vendor. That the vendor exists, it's not blocked, and the GSTIN on the invoice matches what we have in vendor master. And bank details, if the invoice shows different bank details from what is in SAP we do not touch it. We raise a ticket to the vendor master team in ServiceNow and keep the invoice on hold. That's a fraud control, they call the vendor back on the registered number.
How often does that happen, the bank detail thing?
Not often. A few times a month maybe. But it's the one we are most careful about.

Then duplicate check. I search in SAP, FBL1N, by vendor and the invoice number, and also in the tracker. SAP also gives a warning if the same reference is already posted. Then if it's a PO invoice I go to MIRO, enter the invoice date, reference, amount, tax code, and the PO number. SAP pulls the PO lines and the goods receipt. I check quantities and price, and if everything matches within tolerance I post it.
What is the tolerance?
Two percent on price. Policy says two percent or five thousand rupees, whichever is lower. Quantity has to match the GR exactly, we don't pay for more than what was received.

After posting I attach the PDF to the SAP document, through the services for object button, create attachment. And then I go back to the tracker and mark it posted with the SAP document number. Then it's in the queue for the payment run.
And the payment run itself, is that AP?
No, treasury runs F110, twice a week, Tuesdays and Fridays. That is outside this process. Our job ends when the invoice is posted and released for payment.
OK, I'll note payment run as out of scope. How long does a clean invoice take you, Sunita?
A clean PO invoice, ten to twelve minutes if SAP is fast. Opening, saving, tracker, checks, MIRO, attaching. The ones with problems take much longer, Karthik will have better numbers on those.
And non-PO invoices, how are those different?

For non-PO we need approval first. We email the invoice to the cost centre owner and ask them to approve. Depending on amount it may need more approvals, that's the delegation of authority. Once they reply approved, I save the approval email as PDF in the same SharePoint folder, then I enter the invoice in FB60 with the GL account and cost centre, and post. The GL account is sometimes tricky, we look at what we used last time for that vendor.
And if there is no last time, a new vendor?
Then we ask the approver or Karthik. There's no fixed rule, honestly. It depends.
OK. Meera, what would you say are the main problems today?

Three things. First, cycle time. From receipt to posting we average around nine days. That hurts us with MSME vendors, because we have to pay micro and small enterprises within forty-five days, and when invoices sit for two weeks before posting we cut it close. Second, we lose early payment discounts. About thirty vendors offer two percent if we pay within ten days, and we almost never make it. Third, the team spends most of its time on typing and chasing, not on checking. Everything is keyed manually into SAP. And the tracker is double work, we maintain it because there is no other way to see status.
Do you have a target in mind for cycle time?
Under four days would be very good. The SOP says five working days but we don't meet it.
Has anyone tried OCR or scanning tools before?

We had a pilot with an OCR tool in 2024, maybe eight months. It didn't stick. Accuracy on line items was poor for our vendors, the team ended up re-checking everything, so it was not saving time. I don't want to repeat that.
That's useful. So accuracy and trust matter more than raw speed.
Exactly.
Sorry, one more pain point. Password protected PDFs. Some vendors send those and we have to call them for the password.
Noted, thank you.
Hi all, sorry, I was stuck in the audit committee prep. Where are we?
Hi Arjun. We've covered the flow and the main pain points. I wanted to ask you about approvals for non-PO invoices and anything from a controls point of view.

Sure. Delegation of authority for non-PO: up to two lakh rupees the cost centre owner can approve. Above two lakh up to ten lakh, the cost centre owner and the department head. Above ten lakh it comes to me as finance controller. And there's a separate rule in AP that anything five lakh and above gets a second check by the AP team lead before posting, PO or non-PO. That's the four-eyes control.
And how are approvals recorded today?

That is my concern. Approvals are emails. Internal audit raised an observation last year that approval evidence was not consistently attached, some approvals were forwarded chains, some were just "ok" replies, and we couldn't always prove the approver was the right person for that amount. So whatever we do, approval evidence must be clean and linked to the invoice.
Understood. Anything on the regulatory side we should know?

The MSME forty-five day rule, Meera probably mentioned it. Since the tax change, payments to micro and small enterprises beyond forty-five days are not deductible in that year, so late posting has a real cost now. And GST, input credit depends on the vendor's filing, but that reconciliation is a monthly activity, not per invoice. I'd keep that out of this exercise for now.
OK, so GSTR-2B reconciliation is out of scope for now.
For now, yes.
And the UK subsidiary, is that part of this?
No. The UK entity is on Workday Financials and they have their own small AP team. Different system, different process. Let's keep this to India and SAP.
Agreed. I have to drop, sorry. Send me the notes.

Thanks Arjun. Meera, Sunita, I'll set up a deep dive on exceptions with Karthik and someone from procurement, and a separate call with SAP and IT on what the system can do. Can you also send me a few sample invoices, with any personal or bank data masked?
Yes, I'll ask Sunita to pick ten, mixed PO and non-PO.
Perfect. Thanks everyone.

Thanks for making time. Karthik, Neha, this is the second session on AP invoice processing. Last week we did the overall flow with Meera and Sunita. Today I want to go deep on the exceptions, because I'm told that's where most of the effort goes.
Yes, that's where the time goes. Happy to go through it.
How many invoices end up as exceptions, roughly?

From the tracker, last quarter about twenty-eight percent of invoices had at least one exception. So more than a quarter. A clean invoice is ten, twelve minutes. An exception invoice is more like thirty-five to forty minutes of actual work, spread over days because we are waiting on people.
What are the biggest exception types?

Number one by far is missing goods receipt. The invoice comes before stores has posted the GR in SAP. That's maybe forty percent of all exceptions. Then price variance, around a quarter. Then quantity differences, maybe ten percent. Then non-PO approvals that are stuck. Then smaller ones: GSTIN mismatch, wrong legal entity on the invoice, duplicates, password-protected PDFs. And the bank detail changes, those are rare but we treat them very seriously.
Let's take missing GR first. What do you do?

When I enter it in MIRO and there's no GR, I park the invoice in MIR7 so it is in SAP but not posted. Then I email the requester or the stores team with the PO number and ask them to post the GR. In the tracker I set status to Waiting GR. If nothing happens in three working days I send a reminder. After seven working days I escalate to Karthik.
And I escalate to the plant stores manager. Sometimes the goods were received but nobody did the MIGO. Sometimes the goods really didn't arrive, and then the invoice shouldn't be paid anyway.
Who decides that the goods really didn't arrive? Is that AP?
No, stores confirms that. We just wait. If stores says not received, we put the invoice on hold and tell the vendor.
OK. Price variance next. Neha, this is where procurement comes in?

Yes. When the invoice price is higher than the PO price beyond tolerance, AP sends us an email with the PO and the invoice. Then the buyer has to look at it. Sometimes the PO price is wrong, because a price revision was agreed and nobody updated the PO, so we amend the PO in ME22N and AP can post. Sometimes the vendor has charged wrong, freight added, an old rate, and then we ask the vendor for a credit note or a revised invoice. That's a judgment call by the buyer, it depends on the contract and what was agreed.
How quickly do buyers usually respond to AP?
Honestly it varies a lot. There's no agreed turnaround. Some buyers respond same day, some take a week.
That's one of our biggest waits, to be honest.
What tolerance is SAP applying today for price?
Policy is two percent or five thousand rupees, whichever is lower. I assume SAP is set to the same, I've never checked the configuration myself.
OK, I'll confirm that with the SAP team on Tuesday. And quantity?

Quantity must not be more than GR quantity. If the invoice is for more than was received, it's the same as missing GR for the difference, we park and ask stores. If the invoice is for less, partial invoice, that's fine, we post what is invoiced.
And when you park for variance, is that MIR7 again?
Yes, park in MIR7 with a note. One annoying thing, sometimes MIRO says the PO is locked because the buyer has it open in ME22N. Then we just wait and try again later.
Non-PO approvals next. What gets stuck?

We email the cost centre owner. If no reply in two working days we send a reminder. After five working days we escalate to the finance controller's office. The problem is people reply from their phones with 'ok', or forward it to someone else who replies, and then we have to work out if that person is allowed to approve that amount. Audit flagged this last year.
Do you have the approver list somewhere, who can approve what?

The delegation of authority matrix is a PDF from finance. The cost centre owners are in SAP against each cost centre. But the department heads, that mapping is not maintained anywhere properly. We use an Excel that I keep.
And what about rejected approvals?
Rare. If the owner says it's not theirs or not valid, we return it to the vendor or forward to the right person. We mark it rejected in the tracker.
GSTIN mismatch and wrong legal entity?

If the vendor GSTIN on the invoice doesn't match vendor master, or our GSTIN is wrong, or it is addressed to the UK company instead of the India company, we cannot post. We return it to the vendor asking for a corrected invoice. Same standard email template, we just change the reason.
Duplicates, how do they happen?

Vendors resend the same invoice, by email and then again by courier, or they send a reminder with the invoice attached. Our rule is same vendor, same invoice number and same gross amount means duplicate. If we suspect one we check the original posting and if it's really a duplicate we don't post it, mark it duplicate in the tracker and tell the vendor it's already in process.
And the high value review you mentioned, Arjun said five lakh and above?

Yes, anything five lakh and above I review before it's posted. I look at the invoice, the PO or approval, the GL coding, the tax. Then I tell the clerk to post. It's a few a day. That one I'd want to keep with a person even if everything else is automated.
Makes sense. And credit notes from vendors, are they the same flow?
Similar but not the same, they have to be matched against the original invoice. Can we do that in a separate session? It's a smaller volume.
Sure, I'll park credit notes for now. Anything else that takes a lot of time?
Vendor follow-ups. Vendors call and email asking for payment status. We look in the tracker and SAP and reply. That's maybe an hour a day for the whole team, but it's not really invoice processing.
I'll note vendor status queries as related but out of scope for this assessment. Thank you all, this was very helpful.
AP Invoice Processing - SAP and integration review
Tuesday 14 October 2026, 15:00-15:45 IST (Zoom)
Attendees: Rahul Deshpande (Automation CoE, BA), Vikram Shah (SAP FI/MM functional lead), Daniel Fernandes (Integration architect), Ananya Bose (IT security)
Transcript exported from Zoom. Lightly cleaned; filler words removed.

Thanks for joining. Short context: we're assessing AP invoice processing for the India entity. I want to understand what the systems can do today, so that any recommendation is grounded in what actually exists, not what we hope exists.

Sure. So, landscape first. India runs on SAP S/4HANA 2022, on-premise, company code 1000. AP uses SAP GUI mostly, MIRO, MIR7, FB60, FBL1N. Some people use the Fiori Manage Supplier Invoices app but most of the AP team is on GUI.
Are there APIs we could use to create supplier invoices instead of keying them in MIRO?

Standard S/4 has the supplier invoice OData API, API_SUPPLIERINVOICE_PROCESS_SRV. It can create and post supplier invoices with PO reference. But we have not activated it in our Gateway. Nobody has needed it so far.

And even once it's activated in Gateway, nothing is exposed to other systems without going through our API management layer. That's a change request, security review, a technical user with the right authorisations. Realistically four to six weeks if it is prioritised. I wouldn't promise it until we raise the request and see.
Understood, so the API exists in the product but isn't available to us today.
Correct. Available in the product, not available in our landscape.
What about reading purchase orders?
That one is live. API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV is exposed through API management for the supplier portal project, read only. We can give another consumer read access with a normal access request.
Goods receipts?
For GRs there is the material document API, API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV. I think the warehouse team activated it last year for their scanners, but I'm not sure if it's exposed outside. I need to check.
OK, I'll mark that as to be confirmed. Vendor master?
Business partner read, API_BUSINESS_PARTNER, is live through API management. The MDM team uses it. Read only.
And attaching the PDF to the SAP document, can that be done through an API?
There is an attachment API in S/4, but I've never set it up here. I don't know if it's active. Put it as unknown.
What about UI automation, bots driving SAP GUI?

SAP GUI scripting is disabled on production by policy. It's been like that since go-live. Enabling it needs a security exception approved by the CISO, and we would rather not. If there's an API path, that's our preference, much easier to control and audit.
That's a clear steer. And the mailbox?

The ap.invoices shared mailbox is in Microsoft 365. We already read it through Microsoft Graph for the vendor statement bot, there's an app registration with mail read permission scoped to that mailbox. SharePoint, same, we have Graph access to the AP Invoices library. So email and SharePoint are both doable today.
Good. Vikram, one specific thing. What price tolerance is configured for invoice verification in company code 1000?

Let me check, I have the system open. Tolerance key PP, price variance... it's set to five percent upper and five percent lower. No absolute amount limit configured. I don't think anyone has changed it since go-live.
Interesting. AP told me policy is two percent or five thousand rupees, whichever is lower.
Then the configuration doesn't match the policy. SAP will accept up to five percent without blocking. I'd raise that with Meera, it's a control gap regardless of automation.
I will. And the duplicate check in SAP?
Standard duplicate invoice check is on for company code 1000. It checks vendor, reference number and invoice amount. It gives a warning, not an error, so a clerk can still post.

Can I add something on data? Invoices have vendor bank account numbers and sometimes personal data for individual consultants. Our classification for that is Confidential. If any extraction or AI service is used, the data has to stay in an approved region, India or an approved cloud region, and the service has to go through vendor risk assessment. No sending invoices to random online tools.
Understood, I'll note that as a constraint.
Last one, the vendor master change tickets go into ServiceNow. Is there any integration there?
Not that I know of for AP. That's a question for the ServiceNow team.
OK. And the UK entity is on Workday, I assume nothing changes there?
Right, Workday is separate, not our team.
Great. I'll send a summary with the open items: GR API exposure, attachment API status, ServiceNow integration, and the tolerance gap. Thanks everyone.

Vendor Invoice Processing (India)
Document ID | SOP-FIN-AP-004
Version | 3.2
Effective date | 1 April 2026
Process owner | Meera Iyer, Manager - Accounts Payable
Approved by | Arjun Malhotra, Finance Controller
Next review | 31 March 2027
1. Purpose

This procedure defines how vendor invoices received by Kaveri Industrial Components Ltd. (company code 1000) are recorded, validated, approved and posted in SAP S/4HANA so that suppliers are paid accurately and on time and statutory requirements are met.
2. Scope
In scope:
Purchase-order (PO) and non-PO vendor invoices for company code 1000 (India).
Invoices received by email at ap.invoices@kaveri-ic.example and paper invoices received at the Pune office.
Out of scope:
Payment runs (F110), performed by Treasury under SOP-FIN-TR-002.
Vendor master creation and changes, performed by the Vendor Master Data team under SOP-FIN-MD-001.
Employee expense claims, processed in SAP Concur.
Kaveri UK Ltd., which uses Workday Financials.
Month-end GR/IR clearing and accruals, and monthly GST input credit reconciliation (GSTR-2B).
3. Definitions
Term | Meaning
PO invoice | An invoice that references a purchase order in SAP.
Non-PO invoice | An invoice without a purchase order, e.g. utilities, rent, professional fees.
GR | Goods receipt posted in SAP (MIGO) for a purchase order.
Three-way match | Comparison of invoice, purchase order and goods receipt for quantity and price.
Park | Saving an invoice in SAP (MIR7) without posting it.
DoA | Delegation of Authority matrix issued by Finance.
MSE | Micro or small enterprise registered under the MSMED Act, 2006.
4. Roles and responsibilities
Role | Responsibilities
AP Clerk | Logs, validates, enters, parks and posts invoices; requests GRs and approvals; attaches invoice images; maintains the AP tracker.
AP Team Lead | Reviews invoices of INR 5,00,000 and above before posting; handles escalations; maintains the approver mapping.
AP Manager | Owns this SOP; monitors KPIs; resolves policy questions.
Requester / Stores | Posts goods receipts in SAP; confirms whether goods or services were received.
Buyer (Procurement) | Resolves price and quantity variances: amends the PO or obtains a credit note or revised invoice from the vendor.
Cost Centre Owner and DoA approvers | Approve non-PO invoices within their authority.
Vendor Master Data team | Verifies and applies any vendor master change, including bank details, after a call-back to the vendor.
5. Policy rules

5.1 Price tolerance: an invoice may be posted when the unit price differs from the PO price by no more than 2% or INR 5,000 per invoice, whichever is lower. Larger differences must be resolved by the Buyer before posting.
5.2 Quantity: the invoiced quantity must not exceed the quantity received (GR). No tolerance applies.
5.3 Duplicates: an invoice with the same vendor, the same invoice number and the same gross amount as an invoice already recorded in the same financial year is a duplicate and must not be posted.
5.4 Four-eyes review: every invoice with a gross amount of INR 5,00,000 or more must be reviewed by the AP Team Lead before posting.

5.5 Bank details: AP must not process an invoice whose bank details differ from the vendor master. The change is routed to the Vendor Master Data team, which verifies it by calling the vendor on the registered number.
5.6 Non-PO approvals follow the DoA thresholds below. Approval evidence must be saved with the invoice.
5.7 Invoices must be addressed to Kaveri Industrial Components Ltd. and show its GSTIN and the vendor GSTIN registered in the vendor master.
Table 1. DoA thresholds for non-PO invoices
Gross invoice amount (INR) | Required approval
Up to 2,00,000 | Cost Centre Owner
Above 2,00,000 up to 10,00,000 | Cost Centre Owner and Department Head
Above 10,00,000 | Cost Centre Owner, Department Head and Finance Controller
6. Procedure
6.1 Receive invoice
Vendors send invoices as PDF to ap.invoices@kaveri-ic.example. Paper invoices received at the Pune office are scanned by the AP Clerk on the office scanner and sent to the same mailbox.
6.2 Log the invoice

Save the PDF in the vendor folder of the SharePoint library "AP Invoices" and record it in the AP tracker (vendor, invoice number, invoice date, gross amount, PO number, date received, status "Received").
6.3 Check mandatory fields

Confirm the invoice shows: Kaveri legal name and GSTIN; vendor name and GSTIN; invoice number and date; PO number (PO invoices); HSN/SAC codes; taxable value and tax breakup. If any item is missing or wrong, or the invoice is addressed to another legal entity, return it to the vendor using template AP-T01 and set status "Returned".
6.4 Validate the vendor

In SAP (transaction BP), confirm the vendor exists, is not blocked for posting and that the GSTIN matches. If bank details on the invoice differ from the vendor master, follow rule 5.5: raise a ServiceNow request to Vendor Master Data and set status "On hold - vendor master".
6.5 Check for duplicates
Search SAP (FBL1N) and the AP tracker by vendor and invoice number. Apply rule 5.3. If the invoice is a duplicate, do not post; set status "Duplicate" and inform the vendor.
6.6 Enter PO invoices

Enter the invoice in MIRO with reference to the PO. If no GR exists for the invoiced quantity, park the invoice (MIR7), email the requester or stores to post the GR and set status "Waiting GR". Send a reminder after 3 working days and escalate to the AP Team Lead after 7 working days.
6.7 Resolve variances

If SAP shows a price or quantity variance beyond rules 5.1 or 5.2, park the invoice, email the Buyer with the PO and invoice, and set status "Variance". The Buyer either amends the PO or obtains a credit note or revised invoice from the vendor.
6.8 Approve non-PO invoices

Email the invoice to the approver(s) required by Table 1. Send a reminder after 2 working days and escalate to the Finance Controller's office after 5 working days. Save the approval email as PDF in the vendor folder.
6.9 Enter non-PO invoices
Enter the approved invoice in FB60 with the GL account and cost centre.
6.10 Four-eyes review
For invoices of INR 5,00,000 or more, the AP Team Lead reviews the invoice, PO or approval, GL coding and tax before posting (rule 5.4).
6.11 Post and attach
Post the invoice. Attach the invoice PDF to the SAP document using Services for Object > Create Attachment.
6.12 Close the record
Update the AP tracker with the SAP document number and status "Posted". Posted invoices are released for the Treasury payment run.
The process flow is shown in Appendix A (AP-Invoice-AsIs.drawio).
7. Exception handling
Exception | Action | Owner
Missing or incorrect mandatory field | Return to vendor (template AP-T01) | AP Clerk
Invoice addressed to another legal entity | Return to vendor | AP Clerk
Bank details differ from vendor master | Hold; ServiceNow request to Vendor Master Data | AP Clerk / Vendor Master Data
Suspected duplicate | Do not post; confirm with vendor | AP Clerk
No goods receipt | Park; request GR; remind at 3 and escalate at 7 working days | AP Clerk / Requester
Price or quantity variance | Park; refer to Buyer | Buyer
Non-PO approval not received | Remind at 2 and escalate at 5 working days | AP Clerk / AP Team Lead
Password-protected or unreadable PDF | Request a readable copy from the vendor | AP Clerk
8. Records
Invoices, approvals and supporting documents are retained for eight years from the end of the financial year to which they relate.
9. Performance measures
Measure | Target
Cycle time, receipt to posting | 5 working days or less
Invoices posted without exception (first pass) | 80% or more
MSE invoices paid within 45 days | 100%
Volume reference: approximately 8,500 invoices per month (FY 2025-26 average).
10. Revision history
Version | Date | Change | Author
3.0 | 1 April 2024 | Added rule 5.5 (bank details call-back). | Meera Iyer
3.1 | 1 October 2025 | DoA thresholds updated. | Meera Iyer
3.2 | 1 April 2026 | Four-eyes threshold set to INR 5,00,000; escalation timings added. | Meera Iyer
